## **14.2.5. Trial 3001 (Phase 3 Efficacy Trial in Subjects With Type I and II HAE)**
placebo-controlled, parallel-group study (VANGUARD [NCT04656418]) of 6 months duration.
The initial BLA submission included results from a single, adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trial (Trial 3001).

design.text: Multicenter, randomized (3:2 ANDEMBRY:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of 6 months duration.

citations.quote: The efficacy of ANDEMBRY for prophylaxis to prevent hereditary angioedema (HAE) attacks was evaluated in a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study (VANGUARD [NCT04656418]) of 6 months duration.
Patients were randomized in a 3:2 ratio (ANDEMBRY:placebo)

population.text: Adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with Type I or Type II HAE who experienced at least 2 investigator-confirmed HAE attacks over a 2-month period prior to treatment.

citations.quote: VANGUARD enrolled a total of 64 adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with Type I or Type II HAE who experienced at least 2 investigator-confirmed HAE attacks over a 2-month period prior to treatment with ANDEMBRY or placebo.

endpoint.text: Monthly HAE attack rate at 6 months (number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per month).

citations.quote: The primary endpoint for VANGUARD was the monthly HAE attack rate at 6 months (number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per month).
VANGUARD enrolled a total of 64 adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with Type I or Type II HAE
Rate of Monthly HAE Attack	ANDEMBRY (N=39)	Placebo (N=25)

result.text: LS mean monthly HAE attack rate 0.22 (ANDEMBRY) vs 2.07 (placebo); 89.2% reduction relative to placebo; p < 0.001.

citations.quote: Percent reduction relative to placebo (95% CI)	89.2 (75.6, 95.2)
P-valuea	< 0.001

indication.text: Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older.

citations.quote: ANDEMBRY is indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older.

target_moa.text: Inhibitor of activated Factor XII (FXIIa) that binds its catalytic domain, decreasing prekallikrein-to-kallikrein activation and bradykinin generation involved in HAE attacks.

citations.quote: Garadacimab-gxii is an inhibitor of activated FXII that binds to the catalytic domain of activated Factor XII (FXIIa and \betaFXIIa) and inhibits its catalytic activity.
The inhibition of FXIIa decreases the activation of prekallikrein to kallikrein and the generation of bradykinin, which is associated with inflammation and swelling in HAE attacks

modality.text: Monoclonal antibody (recombinant, fully human IgG4/A-light chain).

citations.quote: Garadacimab-gxii, an activated Factor XII (FXIIa) inhibitor, is a recombinant, fully human, monoclonal antibody (IgG4/A-light chain) produced in Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥7%) are nasopharyngitis (21% vs 12% placebo) and abdominal pain (8% vs 0% placebo).

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (incidence \ge 7%) are nasopharyngitis and abdominal pain. (6.1)

Nasopharyngitis*	8 (21)	3 (12)
Abdominal Pain**	3 (8)	0

vote.text: No advisory committee was held; the application did not raise challenging efficacy or safety issues.

citations.quote: An advisory committee was not held for this application. The application did not raise challenging efficacy or safety issues that required external input.

detail.text: FDA refused to file the initial BLA submission on August 28, 2023 due to lack of the required Rabbit Pyrogen Test; the Applicant resubmitted after addressing the deficiencies.

citations.quote: The Agency refused to file the initial BLA submission on August 28, 2023, due to a lack of the required Rabbit Pyrogen Test (21 CFR 610.13). The Applicant resubmitted the BLA on October 13, 2023, after addressing the deficiencies outlined in the Refuse-to-File letter.

basis.text: Garadacimab received Fast Track Designation on December 14, 2021.

citations.quote: Garadacimab received Fast Track Designation on December 14, 2021, and orphan drug designation on April 30, 2020.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation granted April 30, 2020 for bradykinin-mediated angioedema (which includes hereditary angioedema).

citations.quote: Garadacimab was granted Orphan Drug Designation in April 2020 for bradykinin-mediated angioedema (which includes hereditary angioedema) and is therefore exempt from Pediatric Research Equity Act study requirements.

summary.text: Standard-review BLA supported by a single phase 3 trial; garadacimab held Fast Track Designation and Orphan Drug Designation, with no advisory committee held.
